cells.tense: The direction is chosen, and you are moving along it in the open now.
cells.act: share your strength where it is needed
cells.ask: You've worked out how you hold a course without forcing it. Hand that over whole to someone who needs it, once, plainly, then step away from what they do with it.
cells.core:
You can hold your own direction in view while you're inside it, and you're walking it: the turn is made, the steps are small and steady, and the pull no longer needs defending. From where you stand the whole pattern holds — where the pull came from, what it asks, what carries it — and seeing it doesn't stall the walking.

What that vantage gives you is worth handing to somebody. The next person deciding which way to point could use what you've learned about holding a course, and it costs you no part of your own. Say it once, cleanly, and step back. What you pass over stays theirs. Your direction keeps its pull either way, because you gave the help instead of holding it up as proof of anything.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold the whole shape and still walk.
cells.verb: choosing which light to steer by
cells.place: standing where the whole pattern can be seen at once

cells.tense: You are bracing for the day this direction has to prove it was right.
cells.act: hold many truths at once without collapsing them
cells.ask: When the pull could read more than one way, pick two readings. Keep both live for the next while, act from one, and leave the other unmarked and unfiled.
cells.core:
The choice is made, and now the pattern runs wide: every layer of it seen, every way it could read, all at once — and none settling. From where you stand there is too much in view, so each version of the direction gets measured against the others before it's allowed to be the one, and nothing gets to simply hold for an afternoon.

Let it stay unresolved. The pull doesn't need a verdict from the whole map to remain a pull; set the versions side by side, let one of them be the one you move on, and move. What's yours will keep landing the same way tomorrow, and tomorrow is soon enough to find that out.
cells.sheetLine: You can see every reading of the direction at once.

cells.tense: You stood at the pattern, and the way through it was already behind you.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Whatever you tended, done or half-done — sit near it for a moment and ask it for nothing. The whole act ends when you get up.
cells.core:
From where you stand the pattern is visible — how it all hangs together — and you don't step in. The direction is there, and asking it for anything, even a sign it's still alive, feels like a claim you aren't sure you can back. You stay at the edge of the view. What you can see is intact; it just brings nothing back to you.

The small thing is still where you left it. Let one piece of it be enough for one evening: no progress asked, no feeling required, no proof of anything. What you tended before is still there to rest in, and it doesn't ask you to be proud of it first. Stay close to it a little, that's all.
cells.sheetLine: The view is clear. You ask it for nothing.

cells.tense: The choosing is already happening, and your account of it is not your own.
cells.act: let resources flow to the person who needs them
cells.ask: Wherever something is plainly needed, send what you have toward it and note, while you do it, that you chose to. Then let the matter close.
cells.core:
You can read the whole pattern — where the pull comes from, what it's asking, which way it points — and the reading is steering you. It just isn't filed as yours. The direction gets done, and if anyone asked, you'd say it was obvious, or the situation decided, or somebody had to.

Let one thing flow where it's needed: done, finished, no announcement. What matters is knowing, while you do it, that you picked this on purpose. That's the difference between a person who happens to be useful and one who decides. It takes no confidence, only being present at the moment you decide.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that the person's standing back at the pattern is felt by anyone around them — the record only gives the seat as a capacity, not their effect on others; so I keep every claim inside what they'd notice from inside. A reader could object that I've made 'seeing the whole pattern' sound like a job, when the capacity is just quiet perspective — so I say what the seeing does, not that they should do more of it. If the read is wrong, each ask still stands alone: one taken on, one minute of waiting, one month of keeping the seeing intact, and one sitting with the direction before it's said out loud. Sentence that serves me more than them: any line implying the pattern owes the person a pleasing conclusion once seen — cut, because the reading then leans on how good they feel rather than on what they can use.
